questions.qtext: What is the type of microstructure of 0.4 Wt% C steel at 900°C?

options.text: Austenite
Pearlite
Austenite grains and ferrite on grain boundaries
Cementite

questions.solution:
(a)
The eutectoid composition of steel is 0.8 Wt%C, and the eutectoid temperature is 727°C, the
microstructure is fully austenitic, because it’s above the separating austenite from ferrite + Austenite
for hypoeutectoid steels.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: Which of the following are effects of fine austenite grains in steel?

options.text: Improved machinability and surface finish.
Improved creep strength.
Reduced quenching cracks and distortion.
Fine grains, have improvement in strength of steel after heat treatment.

questions.solution:
(a, c, d)
Various physical and mechanical properties of steel depends on the grain size of austenite. If
grains are coarse, creep strength will be improved.
questions.subject: Technical

options.text: Heating the eutectoid steel at a temperature below eutectoid for sufficiently long period.
Moderately cooling the eutectoid steel.
By fast cooling the eutectoid steel.
Heating the eutectoid steel at a temperature above eutectoid for short time period.

questions.solution:
(a)
Steel with pearlite or bainite microstructure is heated and left at a temperature below the eutectoid point for a sufficiently long period of time (18-24h for 700°C) will leads to formation of spheroidite, where Fe3C phase is formed in the shape of sphere-like-particles embedded in a continuous matrix α-ferrite.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is NOT correct for normalizing?

options.text: Normalizing temperatures are lower than annealing.
Normalizing can be done on cast products to eliminate dendritic structure.
Normalizing removes internal stresses developed during forging.
Normalizing is done to improve mechanical properties of steel by grain refinement.

questions.solution:
(a)
Normalizing is done on steels for grain refinement and improvement in mechanical properties.
• Normalizing temperatures are higher than annealing and hardening temperature of steels.
• Steels are held at normalizing temperature for a short duration and then cooled in still air.

questions.qtext: In the standard wringing procedure for slip gauges, which of the following steps is specifically taken to expel air between the gauges and ensure proper adhesion?

options.text: Heating the slip gauges before contact.
Applying oil between the gauge faces.
Bringing the faces into contact at right angles and then sliding one gauge through 90°.
Bringing the faces into contact parallel to each other and then sliding one gauge through 90°.

questions.solution:
(c)
Wringing is the process of joining two slip gauges together such that they stick firmly due to molecular adhesion, surface tension and vacuum (removal of air) between their ultra-smooth surfaces.
